description: Admin Follow-ups — Close the six known gaps from the Admin Backend Overhaul that shipped intent but not the underlying mechanics. (1) Rewire calculate_trending_scores to read from trending_config so the tuner actually changes scoring. (2) Add a scheduler cron that flips newsletter_campaigns rows from scheduled to sent at the right time. (3) Wire up the Resend webhook so newsletter campaigns get real delivery / open / click / bounce numbers instead of zeros. (4) Add a reply thread + Resend-backed admin reply to FeedbackInbox so support conversations don't dead-end in the dashboard. (5) Extend deals with recurring-rule columns (days_of_week, start_time, end_time) and surface them in the DealManager. (6) Replace the dropdown stage-change in PartnershipsManager with drag-to-update kanban via @dnd-kit.

userStories.title: Rewrite calculate_trending_scores to read weights from trending_config
userStories.description: As an admin, when I save new weights in the Trending tuner I need the next scheduled trending recalculation to actually use those weights, not the hard-coded values the dashboard-created SQL function currently has baked in.
acceptanceCriteria: New migration creates (or replaces) public.calculate_trending_scores() — pulls the single row from public.trending_config inside the function and uses each column in the score formula

Score formula at minimum: (views * view_weight) + (favorites * favorite_weight) + (shares * share_weight) + (clicks * click_weight), multiplied by exp(-age_hours / recency_half_life_hours), plus featured_boost when is_featured is true
Rows younger than min_age_hours are excluded from the result (zero score)
Function is SECURITY DEFINER with search_path = public so RLS doesn't trip it
Existing callers continue to work — same return shape (popularity_score column on events) and the calculate-trending edge function does not need changes
Verify by saving a markedly different weight in the tuner, invoking calculate-trending, and asserting popularity_score actually shifts for a known row
Typecheck + lint pass
userStories.notes: SHIPPED: Migration 20260520000011 creates public.calculate_trending_scores() — reads the singleton trending_config row, counts views/clicks/shares/saves from user_event_interactions and 'thumbs_up'+'interested' from user_event_feedback in the last 7 days per event, applies the recency decay (exp(-age_hours / recency_half_life_hours)) with featured_boost added when is_featured, gates rows younger than min_age_hours to zero, and clamps to >=0. SECURITY DEFINER + search_path = public. The calculate-trending edge function continues to work without changes (it calls supabase.rpc('calculate_trending_scores') and ignores the return value, now an INTEGER row count). SCOPE DEVIATION FROM PRD: writes to a NEW events.trending_score column instead of overwriting the existing events.popularity_score. Reason — popularity_score is maintained by a per-row BEFORE UPDATE trigger from 20260506000008 that recomputes a 0-100 structural score (featured + imminence + view_count + saves) on every edit. If this scheduled function wrote popularity_score, the next admin edit would silently revert engagement-weighted scores. The two signals coexist cleanly on separate columns; if a future story wants the public 'Popularity' sort to use engagement-weighted scoring, that's a tiny follow-up that swaps the ORDER BY column. types.ts not updated since no codebase consumer reads trending_score yet.

userStories.title: Cron worker that dispatches scheduled newsletter campaigns
userStories.description: As an admin, when I schedule a newsletter campaign for a future time I need a worker to actually pick it up and send it; right now the row sits with status='scheduled' forever.
acceptanceCriteria: New edge function dispatch-scheduled-newsletters reads newsletter_campaigns where status='scheduled' AND scheduled_for <= now() (limit 5 per run), atomically flips each to status='sending' before dispatching, then calls the existing send pipeline
On success, updates row to status='sent' with sent_at, delivered, failed counts (same shape as send_now in send-newsletter-campaign)
On failure, updates row to status='failed' with error_message (first 500 chars) so it surfaces in the admin Campaigns list
pg_cron schedule registered via migration (minute granularity) — calls the edge function via supabase_url + service-role auth header pattern that send-weekly-digest already uses
Function is admin-callable too so an admin can 'send overdue scheduled' manually from a future button (not required in this story)
Idempotent: a row that's already 'sending' is skipped, never double-dispatched
Typecheck + lint pass
userStories.notes: SHIPPED: New edge function dispatch-scheduled-newsletters reads up to 5 due rows per run via a SECURITY DEFINER RPC public.claim_scheduled_newsletter_campaigns(p_limit) that atomically flips status='scheduled' → 'sending' inside a single UPDATE ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED ... RETURNING. This makes concurrent / duplicate cron firings idempotent (later firings see no claimable rows). Dispatcher then loops the existing Resend send pattern (5/batch via Promise.allSettled) and updates each row with final status='sent' (or 'failed' if zero delivered), sent_at, delivered, failed, and a 500-char error_message digest. Migration 20260520000012 also registers the cron schedule (every minute via pg_cron + net.http_post + service-role bearer) following the established 20250107000006_schedule_event_scraping.sql pattern. Manual admin invocation works the same way for future drain-overdue buttons.

userStories.title: Resend delivery webhook — populate per-recipient delivery rows + campaign tallies
userStories.description: As an admin, I need real open / click / bounce / complaint numbers in the Campaigns list so I can tell whether a newsletter actually landed; right now the table only knows what Resend's accept-time response said.
acceptanceCriteria: New migration creates newsletter_deliveries table: id, campaign_id (FK newsletter_campaigns), email, resend_message_id (unique), status (queued/delivered/opened/clicked/bounced/complained), event_at, error_message, created_at, updated_at. RLS: service_role full, admin SELECT
send-newsletter-campaign now writes one newsletter_deliveries row per recipient at send time with status='queued' and the Resend message id from the API response (Resend returns { id } on 200)

New edge function resend-webhook (verify_jwt=false) verifies the X-Resend-Signature using RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET, updates the matching delivery row by resend_message_id, and increments / decrements the parent campaign tallies (delivered / opens / clicks / bounces / complaints)

newsletter_campaigns gains columns: opens INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, clicks INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, bounces INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, complaints INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 (added via this migration)
Handle the Resend event types we care about: email.delivered, email.opened, email.clicked, email.bounced, email.complained. Other events return 200 + ignore
NewsletterCampaignsManager UI grows two additional columns (Opens, Clicks) on lg+ and surfaces bounce % inline when > 5% with an amber tone
types.ts updated for newsletter_deliveries and the new newsletter_campaigns columns
Document the Resend webhook URL + RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET in the function header so an admin can configure it once
Typecheck + lint pass
userStories.notes: SHIPPED: Migration 20260520000013 (a) adds opens/clicks/bounces/complaints columns to newsletter_campaigns (INTEGER, NOT NULL, default 0), (b) creates public.newsletter_deliveries (one row per recipient per send: id, campaign_id FK CASCADE, email, resend_message_id UNIQUE, status enum queued/delivered/opened/clicked/bounced/complained, event_at, error_message) with service_role-full + admin-SELECT RLS, and (c) creates a SECURITY DEFINER helper bump_newsletter_campaign_counter(p_campaign_id, p_field) so the webhook stays tiny. Both send paths (send-newsletter-campaign send_now + dispatch-scheduled-newsletters) now capture the Resend message_id from the API response and write a delivery row per recipient with status='queued' on success or status='bounced'+error_message on failure. New edge function resend-webhook (verify_jwt=false; Svix signature verified via svix npm package + RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET) handles email.delivered/opened/clicked/bounced/complained — looks up the delivery by resend_message_id, updates status (rank-aware so clicked won't downgrade to delivered on a late event), and calls the RPC to bump the campaign counter. Unknown event types acknowledged 200 to avoid retry storms. Frontend: NewsletterCampaignsManager grew Opens / Clicks columns at lg+ and a Bounce % column at xl+ that turns amber when >5%. Required new secret: RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET (Svix signing key from the Resend dashboard webhook). Configuration steps documented in the resend-webhook header.

userStories.title: Reply thread + admin reply via Resend in FeedbackInbox
userStories.description: As an admin, I need to reply to support messages from the inbox without copying the email address into a separate client; conversations should stay in the admin tool with a visible thread.
acceptanceCriteria: New migration creates feedback_replies table: id, submission_id (FK contact_submissions), direction (admin_to_user|user_to_admin), body_html, sent_by (UUID, admin reply), sent_at, resend_message_id, created_at. RLS: service_role full, admin SELECT/INSERT

New edge function send-feedback-reply: admin-only, takes { submission_id, body_html }, sends via Resend (from same NEWSLETTER_FROM or a new SUPPORT_FROM), records feedback_replies row, updates contact_submissions.status to 'responded' + responded_at
FeedbackInbox detail Sheet shows the reply thread newest-first below the original message; each entry has direction badge, body, timestamp
Reply composer is a textarea + Send button at the bottom of the Sheet; disabled while sending; success appends the new reply to the thread inline
If the customer replies later to the threaded email, that's an out-of-scope follow-up (the table direction column supports it, but inbound mail parsing isn't part of this story)
Typecheck + lint pass
userStories.notes: SHIPPED: Migration 20260520000014 creates public.feedback_replies (id, submission_id FK CASCADE, direction CHECK admin_to_user/user_to_admin default admin_to_user, body_html, sent_by, sent_at, resend_message_id) with service_role-full + admin SELECT/INSERT RLS via is_admin(). New edge function send-feedback-reply (admin-only): looks up the contact_submission, sends Re: <subject> via Resend (SUPPORT_FROM env var or NEWSLETTER_FROM fallback), records a feedback_replies row with the message id, and flips the submission to status='responded' + stamps responded_at if blank. FeedbackInbox Sheet now loads + shows the thread newest-first below the original message: each entry has a direction header chip and timestamp; admin replies use a primary-tinted background, user replies use muted (future-proofs the user_to_admin direction even though inbound mail parsing is still out of scope). Composer is a textarea + 'Send to <email>' button at the bottom of the Sheet; disabled while sending; success appends the new reply via loadReplies() and refreshes the detail badge. body_html rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML — trusted because only admins can insert.

userStories.title: Recurring rules on deals (days_of_week + start/end times)
userStories.description: As an admin, I need to express 'happy hour, Tuesday through Thursday, 4 to 6 pm' on a deal so the public Deals page can show recurring patterns instead of just a date range.
acceptanceCriteria: New migration adds to public.deals: days_of_week TEXT[] (CHECK every element in {mon,tue,wed,thu,fri,sat,sun}), start_time TIME, end_time TIME. All nullable
types.ts updated
DealManager edit dialog gains a 'Recurrence' section: 7 day-of-week toggles + start_time + end_time TIME inputs
List view renders a compact recurrence summary in a new column on lg+ (e.g. 'T-W-Th 4–6pm') when days_of_week is non-empty
Validation: if either start_time or end_time is set, both must be; days_of_week without times is allowed (all-day recurring)
useDeals consumers on the public site keep working — new columns are additive and optional
Typecheck + lint pass
